beats.narration_text: Namaste — I'm Vedanshu Daxesh Patel. Three chapters in, retrieval has gone from a fix to a mechanism. Chapter one made a stale answer current. Chapter two watched the obvious fix fail. Chapter three turned meaning into numbers. Let's put the three together, because the through-line is a single sentence — and it isn't the one most people start with.

props.command: I've built three chapters: retrieval fixing a stale answer, the pasted-manual fix failing, and embeddings turning meaning into vectors. Tie them into one claim about what retrieval actually is.
output: ch1  stale answer -> current, because the document was handed over
ch2  whole manual pasted -> still the wrong paragraph
ch3  meaning becomes a vector; closeness becomes an angle
through-line: retrieval is SELECTION, not volume

beats.narration_text: Here's the whole thing in one breath. Retrieval is not about handing a model more text. It is about choosing which text — and that choice, not the size of the context, is what makes an answer right.

show.event: serif text types on cream: 'Retrieval means giving the model more text.'
the word 'more' turns terracotta and holds — the writer reconsiders
'more' is deleted character by character
'the right' types in its place; the sentence now reads the reel's actual claim

beats.act: ACT 1 — chapter one: hand it the document
beats.narration_text: Chapter one, in one frame. On the left, a model answering from its training snapshot: ten sick days, stated with total confidence, and wrong for eight months. On the right, the same model handed the current policy passage before it answers. Fifteen days, with its receipt. Nothing about the reasoning changed — only what it was given.

show.event: left card fades up: the frozen snapshot and its stale number
terracotta arrow draws toward the right
right card fades up with a terracotta edge: the retrieved passage and its cited number

props.leftSub: answers from what it saw at training — ten sick days, unchanged for eight months after the policy moved
props.rightSub: handed the current policy before answering — fifteen days, and the passage it used

beats.act: ACT 2 — chapter two: the obvious fix fails
beats.narration_text: So hand it everything, then. Chapter two pastes the whole manual in and lets the script scan for whatever looks relevant. Watch what comes back. The question asks about parental leave; the scan returns the vacation paragraph, because that paragraph shares the word leave and happens to come first. The correct passage is in the manual, further down, never reached.

show.event: terracotta spark and the serif cue land at the top
the command prints with a terracotta dollar sign
the question line prints
the RETRIEVED line prints — visibly the vacation paragraph, not parental leave
the verdict lands quietly: shared word, first match, wrong passage

props.title: python naive_scan.py
lines: Q: How many weeks of parental leave do I get?
Retrieved: Vacation policy: employees accrue 15 vacation days annually. Requests for leave should be submitted two weeks in advance.
A: Based on the manual: employees accrue 15 vacation days annually.

verdict.text: wrong paragraph — it shares the word 'leave', and it came first

beats.act: ACT 3 — chapter three: meaning, not vocabulary
beats.narration_text: Which means the real problem was never how much text. It was which passage — and picking it needs meaning, not word overlap. Chapter three shows it plainly. How much vacation do I get, and what's the PTO policy, share almost no words and land close together. How do I request time off, and how do I request a new laptop, share four words and land far apart.

show.event: spark and headline land; the white plot card fades up
the two terracotta phrasings appear and a connector joins them — close in space
the two ink phrasings appear far apart, despite sharing wording
the redrawn-from-source caption settles at the bottom

props.headline: Same Meaning. Different Words.

beats.narration_text: Once text is a vector, closeness is geometry: the angle between two of them. Cosine similarity — a measure older than embeddings, borrowed from classical information retrieval. That angle is what ranks the passages. Selection stops being keyword luck and becomes a number you can sort on.

show.event: spark and headline land
the question vector draws out from the origin in ink
the passage vector draws out in terracotta
the arc between them appears — the angle that is the score

props.headline: Closeness, Measured
props.caption: cosine similarity — the angle between two vectors (Manning, Raghavan & Schütze, 2008)

beats.narration_text: So here's the verdict across three chapters. Retrieval fixes stale and invented answers by handing the model the current document. Pasting more text does not do that — first-match scanning returns the wrong paragraph. Choosing the right one means comparing meaning as distance. Retrieval is selection, and the selection is the whole job.

show.event: the artifact page opens in the Claude window
the four verdict lines print in order as the voice reaches each

props.artifactHeading: What three chapters add up to
artifactLines: Retrieval fixes stale and invented answers by handing over the current document — the model's reasoning never changed (ch. 1).
More text is not retrieval: a pasted manual scanned for the first keyword match still returns the wrong paragraph (ch. 2).
Choosing the right passage needs meaning, not word overlap — shared wording is not shared meaning (ch. 3).
Text becomes a vector and closeness becomes an angle, so selection becomes a number you can rank on (ch. 3).
Retrieval is selection. The selection is the whole job.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: 'Take a question from my own work and three candidate passages — two that share wording with the question, one that shares only the meaning. Rank them the way keyword search would, then the way embeddings would, and explain where the two orderings disagree and why.' Run it, because the disagreement is the lesson. The place those two rankings split is exactly where retrieval stops being search and starts being meaning. Watch which passage keyword matching puts first.
